I5.quote: Various MOFs with tailored nanoporosities have recently been developed as potential storage media for CO2 and H2.

notes: I1 is met for the MOF and MOF-GO composite samples: H2 uptake at 77 K, 42 atm by a commercial PCI (pressure-composition isotherm) unit; the paper does not use the word volumetric for the H2 measurement, but a PCI unit is a pressure-based volumetric instrument. I2 fails because no H2-measured sorbent has carbon as its majority component by mass (protocol section 3: MOFs are not carbon sorbents). Composition: 'The added GO consisted of 3, 9 and 15 wt% of the material weight, we assume that Cu-BTC was formed in 100% yield.' (main, PDF p. 2, journal p. 819, Materials). The remainder is Cu-BTC (HKUST-1), a MOF. GO alone appears only in the CO2 isotherms (Fig. 6, PDF p. 4) and N2/BET work, not in the H2 data (Fig. 7 legend: Cu-BTC, CG-3, CG-9, CG-15; Table 1 has no GO row). I3, I4, I5 are met but refer to MOF-majority samples. SI (si1) holds only structure, SEM/TEM, FT-IR, TGA and CO2/CH4/N2 figures; no H2 data. Not retracted (record.json is_retracted false; no retraction notice in text). Primary research Communication. No statement that H2 values were published before.
